To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
loss of cofilin 2 (cfl2) disturbs actin dynamics, adhesion between DEL-EVL, and cell migration during gastrulation in Zebra fish.
cofilin  1 is required for the epiboly movement during zebrafish gastrulation.
cofilin 2 is required for proper adhesion and movement of the deep layer during gastrulation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that regulate the epibolic movements during zebrafish gastrulation.
the molecular mechanisms of actin dynamics and cellular junctions during gastrulation.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the epibolic movements of DEL and the associated EVL during gastrulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cfl1 is essential to maintain actin filaments and adhesion between cell layers, which is required for proper cellular movement during gastrulation.
Cfl1 regulates the actin turnover and the actin turnover is essential for the cell adhesion and migration during zebrafish gastrulation.
cfl1 is required for proper actin turnover and cell movements, and the disruption of actin turnover in cfl1 morphant causes the loss of adhesions between DEL and EV L, and cell migration defect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Cfl1 is required to maintain the adhesion between the DEL and the EVL and that this adhesion is essential to maintain coordinated movements of the DEL and the overlying EVL during epiboly.

the loss of cofilin 2 in the DEL and cofilin 4 in the EVL causes the disruption of the actin cytoskeleton, and the dissociation of the DEL and EVL, which in turn causes the failure of cell migration and the subsequent defects in gastrulation.
cfl1 knockdown in the DEL disrupts actin dynamics, adhesion between layers and cell migration during gastrulation in the zebrafish.
The main takeaway from our work is that
actin dynamics mediated by Cfl-1 is important for adhesion between enveloping and deep cell layers and cell movements during epiboly in Zebrafishes.
the actin depolymeric factor, cofilins, is essential for the proper movement of deep cell layers in zebrafishes during gastrulation.
actin turnover is essential for the coordinated movement of the deep and enveloping cell layers during gastrulation in the zebrafish.
